- [LDET.1.8.3] **Cache reads with concurrent writers.** Cache is shared
  mutable state. If two tiers (or two activations, or two
  processes) write the same key in quick succession, the
  order in which those writes land affects what a
  subsequent `cache-get` returns. In live mode that order
  can depend on scheduling, process placement, and wire
  latency — not deterministic. In replay, every cache
  write is recorded as part of the event trace in a
  canonical total order ([RFCS.15.7]), so the sequence is
  fixed. A read is not recorded: it is a pure internal read
  of the engine's cache, re-derived from the writes before
  it ([LFST.5.1]). In simulation, the harness controls the
  ordering directly.
